chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to us, from Ahmad and Muhammad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Badr ibn al-Khalil al-Asadi, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), and he mentioned two signs that would occur before the rising of the Qa'im, which had not occurred since Allah sent Adam down (to earth). He said that the sun would be eclipsed in the middle of the month of Ramadan and the moon in its end. A man said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, rather it is the sun in the end of the month and the moon in the middle.' Abu Ja'far said to him: 'I know what I am saying. They are two signs that have not occurred since Adam descended.'

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Twelfth Imam (AS) who will rise to establish justice

ai.seo_question: What are the two celestial signs mentioned to appear before the rise of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifies a unique celestial configuration—solar and lunar eclipses occurring in the middle and end of Ramadan respectively—as a definitive sign preceding the rise of al-Qa'im, emphasizing its rarity since the descent of Adam. This narration, recorded by al-Nu'mani, underscores the eschatological significance of these astronomical events as divine markers, distinguishing the era of the Hidden Imam from previous prophetic histories.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (45) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan at-Taymali from Ahmad and Muhammad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father from Tha’laba bin Maymoon that Badr bin al-Khaleel al-Asadi had said:

“Once I was with Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) and he said that two signs would appear before the appearance of al-Qa’im that had never appeared since Allah had sent Adam down to the earth. He said that the sun would be eclipsed in the middle of Ramadan and the moon would be eclipsed in the end of Ramadan. A man said: “O son of the messenger of Allah, it is the moon that will be eclipsed in the middle of Ramadan and the sun will be eclipsed in the end of it.” Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) said: “I do know what I say. They are two signs that have never occurred since Adam (as) has descended to the earth.”
